title: Manipulating Styles with jQuery
summary: Covers the jQuery .css() getter/setter and the class methods addClass, removeClass and hasClass, arguing that toggling classes is cleaner than setting inline styles because it keeps behaviour and appearance separate.

concepts.heading: .css() as setter and getter
points: $("h1").css("color", "green") sets a CSS property: first argument is the property name, second the value, both as strings.
With only one argument, $("h1").css("color") reads the current value instead. For colour, the result is an rgb(...) string (black appears as rgb(0, 0, 0)).
Reading "font-size" returns the computed size in pixels (32px for a default h1 in the demo).
Rule of thumb: one argument gets, two arguments set.

concepts.heading: Keep concerns separate: use classes
points: Setting styles from JavaScript mixes appearance into behaviour code. Preferred split: HTML for content, CSS for appearance, JS for behaviour.
Define a class in the stylesheet (demo: .big-title with a large font-size, yellow colour and cursive font-family) and let jQuery attach it.
$("h1").addClass("big-title") adds the class; $("h1").removeClass("big-title") takes it away and the rule's styles disappear.
To add or remove several classes in one call, put them in a single string separated by spaces: addClass("big-title margin-50").
$("h1").hasClass("margin-50") returns true or false depending on whether the element carries that class.
(Extra) toggleClass("name") adds the class if absent and removes it if present; handy with event handlers.

code_examples.caption: style.css
script.js: css(), addClass, removeClass, hasClass

pitfalls: Separate multiple class names with a space inside ONE string, not as separate arguments or with dots.
Do not put a dot before the class name in addClass/removeClass/hasClass (use "big-title", not ".big-title").
The reference repo calls removeClass before the class has been added; harmless but not what the lecture sequence shows.

gaps_and_ideas: Lesson 'jQuery styles and classes'. Tasks: set h1 colour with css(); read two properties; create a .big-title class and add it; add two classes at once; log hasClass before and after removal. Demo: buttons that call addClass/removeClass/toggleClass on a preview heading and print hasClass results.
